title.narrative: Mapped in Bangladesh (MiB) IATI Reporting: July 2021 - March 2022

description.narrative: Mapped in Bangladesh (MiB) is a 4-year research initiative by BRAC University that aims to map the export-oriented ready-made garment (RMG) industry across all garment-producing districts in the country. MiB’s design and implementation is in response to the lack of essential sector data, such as, the actual number of factories that exist in the country, the number of male/female workers employed there, the kind of products they produce, the brands that work with them, etc. In line with the nation’s “Digital Bangladesh Vision 2021”, with the MiB tool, the RMG industry is expected to come one step closer to aligning itself to the mandated digitization of every sector. MiB (formerly “DRFM-B” – Digital RMG Factory Mapping in Bangladesh) is being implemented by BRAC University’s Centre for Entrepreneurship Development (CED) and coordinated by BRAC. The project is funded by Laudes Foundation with the co-funding by the Kingdom of the Netherlands (through EKN – Embassy of the Kingdom of the Netherlands). Bangladesh Garment Manufacturers and Exporters Association (BGMEA) and Bangladesh Knitwear Manufacturers and Exporters Association (BKMEA) are the strategic partners of the project. The project is also supported by Department of Inspection for Factories and Establishments (DIFE) under the Ministry of Labour and Employment of the Government of Bangladesh. The project is being coordinated by BRAC.

MiB endeavors to do census of all the export-oriented ready-made garment (RMG) factories in Bangladesh and to provide accurate, credible and updated factory data that can generate various reports for major stakeholders, like brands and buyers, to make informed business decisions.

The key target impact that the project seeks to achieve is the launch of a transparency mechanism used by the industry. This is the first ever project to digitally map the sector and provide an opportunity to understand the universe of export-oriented RMG factories in Bangladesh. The Project, through its mapping and relationship building, will fuel Bangladesh’s RMG industry advancements and inspire shared responsibility and collective action. Mapped in Bangladesh can serve as an example for progress in the global garment industry, by taking into account what is learned in Bangladesh and applying it on an even larger scale. Mapped in Bangladesh strives to ensure the “Made in Bangladesh” brand represents the future of manufacturing ready-made garments, where strengthened and responsible practices are the norm.

The objective of Mapped in Bangladesh is to provide accurate, credible and updated RMG factory information to all industry stakeholders in a manner that enables greater efficiency, productivity, accountability and transparency. Designed and built in Bangladesh, this powerful tool serves as a home-grown solution that further strengthens the country’s significant and thriving RMG industry. The project aims to collect primary data about the export-oriented RMG industry and disclose information to the public in the form of an interactive online map. Driven by a collective action approach, Mapped in Bangladesh seeks input from all stakeholders through its crowd-sourcing platform, in order to keep the data accurate and up-to-date. Because of the growing need for credible, industry-wide data on the number of factories, their locations, number of workers, and much more, challenges remain across the Bangladesh RMG industry. This project is the first of its kind, providing a detailed industry-wide database of export-oriented RMG factories on an interactive, digital map (similar to Google Maps). This new platform is publicly accessible in order to catalyze transparency and bring about meaningful industry improvements in Bangladesh, and thus strengthen the sector as a whole.

title.narrative: Factory Data Collection in Cluster 5 (Rest of the Districts)

description.narrative:
As a part of MiB’s ongoing census of Cluster 5 containing 60 districts all over Bangladesh visited by the Field Officers. During this reporting period and among these 60 districts, MiB Field Officers found export-oriented RMG factories in 17 districts, others have no factories that fit with MiB’s factory definition criteria.
All of the 17 districts have been fully covered (total 80 factories uploaded to the map as of 31 March 2022).

title.narrative: BEPZA Permitted to Share their Member Factory Data

description.narrative:
BEPZA has agreed to share BGMEA and BKMEA member factory data with MiB. MiB has been approaching BEPZA for including their export-oriented RMG factories and a team from MiB also visited the senior BEPZA officials in Dhaka on 31 October 2021 to demonstrate the MiB map. BEPZA authority initially agreed and later sent letters to their 8 zones’ General Managers. As per the GMs’ feedback, BEPZA had an internal meeting and they showed positive attitude towards MiB so far.
On 1 February 2022, BEPZA authority informed that they will share their export-oriented RMG factories’ data with MiB. Follow up in this regard is ongoing.

The Extension of MoU was signed by Mr Miran Ali (Vice President, BGMEA) and Professor Dr Rahim B Talukdar (Adviser – CED & Team Leader – MiB, BracU) on behalf of their respective organizations.
This extension is significant for future collaborations with BGMEA regarding different activities of MiB.

title.narrative: Clusters Covered and Factories Published on the Digital Map

description.narrative:
During this reporting period (1 July 2021 to 31 March 2022), MiB completed uploading factory data of 2 clusters, Cluster 4 (Chattogram District) and Cluster 5 (Rest of the Districts), both in full.
As of March 2022, the map contains a total of 3861 factories from all 5 clusters (Dhaka 1431, Gazipur 1266, Narayanganj 665, Chattogram 419, Other districts 80), of which 2752 are member factories of BGMEA and BKMEA, 1109 are non-member factories.

MiB Crowdsourcing App Developed for Data Update

description.narrative:
MiB developed its “Crowdsourcing App” to update the factory data on the digital map by engaging factory management personnel and workers.
Currently in beta version, the Crowdsourcing App, developed under the MiB project by Brac University, is the gateway to submit and update the RMG factories’ data in a robust and secure way. The app is a useful tool to modify and update the factory data on the digital map. Users can provide factory data by registering with their email address and/or mobile number.
Relevant stakeholders of the RMG sector can utilize the app and update the data directly and effortlessly from their mobile devices.
Initial field testing for Crowdsourcing (i.e. beta testing) started at the end of June 2021, and the App will be updated accordingly as per user’s feedback.
The trained Field Officers (FOs) demonstrated the Crowdsourcing App to the Factory Management(s) and they were quite supportive of the App. At the pilot phase of the app, we received information from 214 factories; among those, 68% (146 factories) have updated the data regularly during the 3-month pilot (as of December 2021).
The FOs conducted the pilot between 29 August to 16 September 2021. A Bangla manual was also developed for the Crowdsourcing App (added to Annex Folder as Annex 1) which the FOs shared with the factory management(s).
The success of the Crowdsourcing App with factory managements would definitely indicate that it could transform the way how data is collected and verified in one of the largest apparel-producing country of the world.
MiB has also been working with factory workers by communicating with different right-based organizations, namely Awaj Foundation, Bangladesh Center for Workers Solidarity (BCWS), and OSH Academy (OHS Initiative for workers and community). MiB plans to pilot the app to create a mechanism to update factory data directly by workers from a particular factory.

title.narrative: Stakeholder Engagement through Project Advisory Committee (PAC) Meeting

description.narrative:
MiB project is the first of its kind to map export-oriented RMG factories across all garment-producing districts in Bangladesh, providing a detailed industry-wide database of factories, including subcontractors, on an interactive, digital map. In order to undertake such a huge challenge – the project is being guided by a multi-stakeholder Project Advisory Committee (PAC), focused on the stakeholder engagement in the from all relevant and essential entities. PAC includes representatives of workers, NGOs, donors, brand/buyers, employers, industry associations, right-based organization, and government representative(s).
The Covid-19 situation hampered organizing the physical Project Advisory Committee (PAC) meeting during this reporting period; though the project was able to organize one virtual PAC meeting on 13 July 2021. At the PAC meeting, MiB has requested the BGMEA and BKMEA representatives to assist the project to gain access to factories located in EPZs to include in the map.

title.narrative: MiB organized the 7th PAC meeting on 13 July 2021.

description.narrative: A Project Advisory Committee (PAC) Meeting of MiB – the 7th PAC Meeting was organized online on 13 July 2021 using the Zoom platform. Several significant topics have been discussed in the PAC Meeting, such as – factory data update, Cluster 5 data collection update, communication with BEPZA, reduction of export percentage of factories and thus include RMG factories exporting below than 80% on a separate map, etc. In terms of getting access to factories located in the EPZs, BGMEA and BKMEA representatives offered assistance to provide data from the factories affiliated with their associations.
